arxiv-2012-01047.title: Systematic Study of Acceleration Efficiency in Young Supernova Remnants with Nonthermal X-ray Observations NuSTARDAS (v1.4.1), HEAsoft (v6.19), nuskybgd (https://github.com/NuSTAR/nuskybgd; Wik et al. 2014 ), XSPEC (v12.9.0, Arnaud 1996 ), CIAO (v4.9, Fruscione et al. 2006 )
arxiv-2012-01047.creator: Naomi Tsuji, Yasunobu Uchiyama, Dmitry Khangulyan, Felix Aharonian
arxiv-2012-01047.description: Abstract Cutoff energy in a synchrotron radiation spectrum of an suprenova remnant (SNR) contains a key parameter of ongoing particle acceleration. We systematically analyze 11 young SNRs, including all historical SNRs, to measure the cutoff energy, thus shedding light on the nature of particle acceleration at the early stage of SNR evolution.

arxiv-2105-07534.title: Slow dynamics for self-adjoint semigroups and unitary evolution groups
arxiv-2105-07534.creator: M. Aloisio, S. L. Carvalho, C. R. de Oliveira, G. Santana
arxiv-2105-07534.description: Abstract We obtain slow dynamics for self-adjoint semigroups and unitary evolution groups. For semigroups, the slow dynamics is for orbits, and for the average return probability in the case of unitary evolution groups. We present an application to the quantum dynamics of purely absolutely continuous systems. 1 Introduction 1.

arxiv-2310-07952.title: Modeling novel physics in virtual reality labs: An affective analysis of student learning
arxiv-2310-07952.creator: Jared P. Canright, Suzanne White Brahmia
arxiv-2310-07952.description: Abstract We report on a study of the effects of laboratory activities that model fictitious laws of physics in a virtual reality environment on (1) students’ epistemology about the role of experimental physics in class and in the world; (2) students’ self-efficacy; and (3) the quality of student engagement with the lab activities.

arxiv-2312-13191.title: Transmuted spectrum-generating algebras and detectable parastatistics of the Superconformal Quantum Mechanics
arxiv-2312-13191.creator: Francesco Toppan
arxiv-2312-13191.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Francesco Toppan. In a recent paper (Balbino-de Freitas-Rana-FT, arXiv:2309.00965) we proved that the supercharges of the supersymmetric quantum mechanics can be statistically transmuted and accommodated into a Z 2 n Z_{2}^{n} -graded parastatistics. In this talk I derive the 6 = 1 + 2 + 3 6=1+2+3 transmuted spectrum-generating algebras (whose respective Z 2 n Z_{2}^{n} gradings are n = 0 , 1 , 2 n=0,1,2 ) of the 𝒩 = 2 {\cal N}=2 Superconformal Quantum Mechanics.

arxiv-2401-02460.title: Improved Zero-Shot Classification by Adapting VLMs with Text Descriptions
arxiv-2401-02460.creator: Oindrila Saha, Grant Van Horn, Subhransu Maji
arxiv-2401-02460.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Oindrila Saha, Grant Van Horn, Subhransu Maji. The zero-shot performance of existing vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP radford2021learning is limited by the availability of large-scale, aligned image and text datasets in specific domains. In this work, we leverage two complementary sources of information—descriptions of categories generated by large language models (LLMs) and abundant, fine-grained image classification datasets—to improve the zero-shot classification performance of VLMs across fine-grained domains. On the technical side, we develop methods to train VLMs with this “bag-level” image-text supervision.

arxiv-2403-10191.title: Generative Region-Language Pretraining for Open-Ended Object Detection
arxiv-2403-10191.creator: Chuang Lin Yi Jiang Lizhen Qu Zehuan Yuan Jianfei Cai
arxiv-2403-10191.description: Abstract In recent research, significant attention has been devoted to the open-vocabulary object detection task, aiming to generalize beyond the limited number of classes labeled during training and detect objects described by arbitrary category names at inference. Compared with conventional object detection, open vocabulary object detection largely extends the object detection categories.

arxiv-2502-11682.title: Double Momentum and Error Feedback For Clipping with Fast Rates and Differential Privacy
arxiv-2502-11682.creator: Rustem Islamov, Samuel Horváth, Aurelien Lucchi, Peter Richtárik, Eduard Gorbunov
arxiv-2502-11682.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rustem Islamov, Samuel Horváth, Aurelien Lucchi, Peter Richtárik, Eduard Gorbunov. Achieving both Differential Privacy (DP) and optimization guarantees is critical For Federated Learning (FL), where client data must remain confidential without compromising model perFormance. However, existing methods typically sacrifice one For the other: they either provide robust DP guarantees at the cost of assuming unrealistic bounded gradients/data heterogeneity assumptions, or they achieve strong optimization rates without any privacy protection .

arxiv-2504-15415.title: IV-Bench: A Benchmark for Image-Grounded Video Perception and Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs
arxiv-2504-15415.creator: M-A-P ByteDance Inc
arxiv-2504-15415.description: Abstract Existing evaluation frameworks for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) primarily focus on image reasoning or general video understanding tasks, largely overlooking the significant role of image context in video comprehension. To bridge this gap, we propose IV-Bench , the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating Image-Grounded Video Perception and Reasoning .

arxiv-2504-20437.title: GaLore 2: Large-Scale LLM Pre-Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
arxiv-2504-20437.creator: DiJia Su, Andrew Gu, Jane Xu, Yuandong Tian, Jiawei Zhao
arxiv-2504-20437.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language understanding and generation but face significant memory bottlenecks during training. GaLore, Gradient Low-Rank Projection, addresses this issue by leveraging the inherent low-rank structure of weight gradients, enabling substantial memory savings without sacrificing performance. Recent works have further extended GaLore in various aspects, including low-bit quantization and higher-order tensor structures.

arxiv-2509-06137.title: Examining the evolution of phase-space elements for C.elegans locomotion
arxiv-2509-06137.creator: Dimitrios Tzepos, Jenny Magnes
arxiv-2509-06137.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios Tzepos, Jenny Magnes. The Caenorhabditis Elegans ( C.elegans ) nematodes have long been a model organism for quantitative behavioral analysis, due to their tractable nervous system and well-characterized genetics. In particular, dynamic diffraction has been a successful method of studying said microorganisms due to its low level of noise and the ability to simultaneously study multiple degrees of freedom of their neuromuscular system through their locomotion.

arxiv-2511-14388.title: Integral Bayesian symbolic regression for optimal discovery of governing equations from scarce and noisy data
arxiv-2511-14388.creator: Oriol Cabanas-Tirapu, Sergio Cobo-Lopez, Savannah E. Sanchez, Forest L. Rohwer, Marta Sales-Pardo, Roger Guimerà
arxiv-2511-14388.description: Abstract Understanding how systems evolve over time often requires discovering the differential equations that govern their behavior. Automatically learning these equations from experimental data is challenging when the data are noisy or limited, and existing approaches struggle, in particular, with the estimation of unobserved derivatives.

arxiv-2601-17437.title: Conformal Quantile Regression for Probabilistic Constitutive Modeling of Anisotropic Soft Materials
arxiv-2601-17437.creator: Bahador Bahmani
arxiv-2601-17437.description: Abstract Biological soft tissues exhibit substantial inter-subject variability, making the automation of constitutive material modeling essential for patient-specific analysis and design. Such materials are not only highly nonlinear but also display intrinsic stochasticity arising from their complex and heterogeneous microstructure.

arxiv-2602-23002.title: Confinement transition to gravitational waves in the one-flavor S ​ U ​ ( 4 ) SU(4) Hyper Stealth Dark Matter theory Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-26-0104-T, IPPP/26/17, SI-HEP-2026-02
arxiv-2602-23002.creator: V. Ayyar, R. C. Brower, G. T. Fleming, J. Ingoldby, X. Y. Jin, N. Matsumoto, A. S. Meyer, E. T. Neil, J. C. Osborn, S. Park, C. T. Peterson, D. Schaich, P. Vranas, O. Witzel, Lattice Strong Dynamics Collaboration
arxiv-2602-23002.description: Abstract The thermodynamics of the S ​ U ​ ( 4 ) SU(4) gauge theory with a single flavor of fundamental quarks is analyzed on the lattice with dynamical fermion simulations, which is the low-energy sector of a realistic, strongly-interacting dark matter model—the Hyper Stealth Dark Matter.

pmc-11378257.title: Optic generation and perpetuation of acoustic bubble clusters
pmc-11378257.creator: Jaka Mur, Fabian Reuter, Vid Agrež, Rok Petkovšek, Claus-Dieter Ohl
pmc-11378257.description: Laser-induced cavitation bubbles offer precise control of the flow in space and time, but they are rarely used for the mechanical and chemical processing of liquids. Instead, strong acoustic fields are commonly used to nucleate and drive cavitation bubbles for liquid process applications.

pmc-11432931.title: Physical Function, Self-Perceived Physical Fitness, Falls, Quality of Life and Degree of Disability According to Fear and Risk of Falling in Women with Fibromyalgia
pmc-11432931.creator: Ángel Denche-Zamorano, Damián Pereira-Payo, Daniel Collado-Mateo, José Carmelo Adsuar-Sala, Pablo Tomas-Carus, Jose Alberto Parraca, Giuseppe Musumeci
pmc-11432931.description: Background: People with fibromyalgia (FM) experience a range of symptoms (chronic widespread pain, fatigue, mood disorder, sleep problems, muscle stiffness) that promote deterioration of physical condition and function. With impaired physical function, fear of falling and risk of falling increases.

pmc-11494386.title: “Circulating Inflammation” and the Plasma Proteome in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
pmc-11494386.creator: Thomas M Vondriska, David J Lefer
pmc-11494386.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Corresponding AuthorKey Words: African Americans, genomics, heart failure with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, proteomics

A heart failure diagnosis characterizes a multi-etiologic syndrome with risk factors including uncontrolled hypertension, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes, and aging. Recent clinical and translational research has focused on the observation that ∼50% of patients exhibit heart failure with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (HFpEF) and not heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

pmc-11668677.title: Nervonic acid alleviates radiation-induced early phase lung inflammation by targeting macrophages activation in mice
pmc-11668677.creator: Chenlin Wang, Yanan Wu, Chao Liu, Yang Li, Song Mi, Xiaofan Yang, Tong Liu, Yuanjing Tian, YingYing Zhang, Pingping Hu, Lili Qiao, Guodong Deng, Ning Liang, Jinyue Sun, Yan Zhang, Jiandong Zhang
pmc-11668677.description: BackgroundPatients receiving chest radiation therapy, or exposed to high radiation levels due to accidental nuclear leakage are at risk of radiation-induced lung injury (RILI). In innate immunity, macrophages not only exhibit certain radiation tolerance but also play an important regulatory role in the whole pathological process.

pmc-12630587.title: Validation of a French version of the DERS-SF and creation of a super short form (DERS-F SSF) for measuring emotion regulation difficulties
pmc-12630587.creator: Simon Thuillard, Noémie Augsburger, Sofia Batziou, Mara Bruni, Laura Fatio, Nahuel Martinez, Elise Mengin, Francesco Ruinato, Livia Sacchi, Natalia Salamon, Mathilde Savary, Elena Trentini, Elise Dan-Glauser
pmc-12630587.description: Difficulties in regulating emotions, i.e., struggling to manage emotions and pursuing goals despite emotions, is a predominant symptom in many diagnoses. In the general population, this variable can be measured with rather comprehensive questionnaires. This is the case of the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS, 36 items), resulting in a total score and six different sub-scores.

pmc-12657315.title: Spillover of Riemerella anatipestifer to laying hens leads to a decrease in egg production and hatchability
pmc-12657315.creator: Wanting Zhou, Xuezhi Cui, Shuning Zhou, Shuo Liu, Cheng Peng, Jizhe Yang, Jinping Li, Guangyu Hou, Wenming Jiang, Hualei Liu
pmc-12657315.description: A strain of Riemerella anatipestifer,a bacterium that primarily infects ducks and geese, was isolated from a layer. Genetic analysis of the housekeeping genes (16S rRNA and rpoB), key virulence genes (prtC, hagA, and sspA), and dominant antigen gene (ompA) revealed that this isolate is closely related to strains commonly found in eastern China.

pmc-12821727.title: Potential of Vagus Nerve Stimulation to Modulate Fibromyalgia’s Network Physiology: A Systematic Review
pmc-12821727.creator: Joao Pedro Perin, Carla Pastora-Sesín, Sungjoon Kang, Alba Navarro-Flores, Felipe Fregni, Kevin Pacheco-Barrios
pmc-12821727.description: Background: Chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) reflect maladaptive network physiology across perceptual–autonomic–immune axes, yet most treatments remain symptomatic and incompletely effective. Methods: We conducted a comprehensive systematic review to evaluate vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) and FMS within a network physiology framework. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched on October 24, 2025.

pmc-12838516.creator: Saparamadu Vipula, Kurera Janakie, Perera W Nirmala
pmc-12838516.description: ObjectivesThe significance of performing tongue brushing is uncertain and lacks sufficient clinical evidence. This study was conducted to assess the existing practices on tongue brushing among school children and their parents and its effect on optimal levels of salt and sugar concentration, the development of dental caries and body mass index among children.ResultsOf 191 students (52.

pmc-13581037.title: Modelling the dark side of prison dynamics: Quantifying the criminogenic effects of petty crime offenders’ incarceration
pmc-13581037.creator: Farai Nyabadza
pmc-13581037.description: Crime remains a persistent socio-economic challenge in South Africa, where the incarceration of petty offenders often exacerbates criminal behaviour. Empirical evidence suggests custodial sentencing for minor offences may accelerate progression to serious crime due to exposure to hardened offenders and criminogenic prison conditions.
